svg.title: the framework guards what reaches the repository: clean commits and no secrets: the commit checks accept clean work and secrets never reach the main branch
svg.text: the framework guards what reaches the repository: clean
Scenario: the commit checks accept clean work and secrets never reach the main branch
The hooks come with the setup, not with the clone
A key is stopped on the laptop
Getting out of a secret block
GitLab is the gate nobody can skip

g.text: Given a project generated from the toolbox sits on GitLab, its commit hooks declared in
lefthook.yml on the main branch
GitLab's page for lefthook.yml on the main branch of a project generated from the toolbox. It declares the commit hooks.
Before each commit, pre-commit runs task betterleaks:protect, a secret scan of the staged files. On each commit message,
commit-msg runs task commitlint:lint-message and task commitizen:check-message.
When a teammate clones it, task dev:setup-environment turns on the commit hooks git never
copies
A teammate clones the project. Git never copies hooks, so ls finds no commit-msg and no pre-commit file in .git/hooks.
task dev:setup-environment is the one-time setup every clone runs, and the dev container runs it on build. The ⋮ stands
for its toolchain checks. Its last phase installs the hooks: lefthook says "sync hooks: ✔️ (commit-msg, pre-commit)",
and ls now finds both files.

text.tspan: git clone http://gitlab/lambda/e2e-commit-hooks.git && cd e2e-commit-hooks && task dev:setup-environment

g.text: Then the hooks refuse the teammate's first commit, the deploy notes under a sloppy message,
with their own explanation
The teammate writes deploy notes on a new branch. deploy/.gitignore ignores *.pem, so git status marks the deploy key
"!!", ignored, and git add stages only the two notes files.
The message has no type. The pre-commit scan passes with "No secrets detected in staged files.", then commitizen and
commitlint both refuse the message. Commitlint says why: "subject may not be empty" and "type may not be empty". No
commit is made.
And the same commit goes through once its message follows the convention, with the
gitignored deploy key left out
The same staged files, with a message that starts with the type "feat:". The scan, commitizen and commitlint all pass,
and git records the commit with its 2 files. The key is not one of them.

text.tspan: git commit -m "feat: add the deploy notes"

g.text: When the teammate stages the deploy key outside its ignored folder, the pre-commit scan
refuses the commit
The teammate copies the key to the root of the project, out of the folder that ignores it, and stages it. cat shows the
fake key in clear.
The pre-commit scan finds a private-key in deploy-key.pem and prints "REDACTED" where the key would be. The commit is
refused: "❌ Betterleaks detected secrets in your staged files!".

text.tspan: cp deploy/deploy-key.pem . && git add deploy-key.pem && git commit -m "chore: add the deploy key"

g.text: When the teammate forces the key past the hook, the branch scan blocks the branch and names
the commit
git commit --no-verify skips the hooks, as the refusal itself pointed out, and the key is committed.
The branch scan reads every commit since the main branch. It names the file and the commit, "chore: add the deploy key",
still prints "REDACTED" instead of the key, and blocks the branch.

text.tspan: git commit --no-verify -m "chore: add the deploy key" && task betterleaks:scan-branch

g.text: When the teammate only deletes the key file, the hooks let the deletion through
The first reflex: delete the key in a new commit. The pre-commit scan reads only what is staged, and a deletion leaves
nothing to read ("scanned ~0 bytes"), so the hooks let the commit through.

text.tspan: git rm deploy-key.pem && git commit -m "chore: remove the deploy key"

g.text: Then the branch scan still finds the key in the commit that added it
The branch has three commits now, and its last version holds no key. The scan still finds it, in the commit "chore: add
the deploy key": deleting a file does not take it out of the history.
When the teammate rewrites the history with the framework's clean-secrets task
task git:clean-secrets removes the file from every commit of the history, not only from the last one. It warns that the
operation is destructive and asks to continue, and the teammate answers yes.
The branch is rewritten: "Ref 'refs/heads/feature/deploy' was rewritten". The key never left this laptop, so nothing on
GitLab needs a force push.
Then the branch scan comes back clean with the deploy notes still on the branch
One commit is left on the branch, the deploy notes. The same scan as two cards before now passes: "No secrets detected
in branch commits."
Then the cleaned branch, pushed as a merge request, passes the same scan on GitLab and is
ready to merge
The teammate pushes the branch, which opens merge request !1. Its pipeline runs the same branch scan, from the same
pinned binary. GitLab shows "Merge request pipeline passed" and "Ready to merge!".

text.tspan: git push -o merge_request.create -o merge_request.target=main origin feature/deploy

g.text: When another branch skips every local check and pushes the key inside a secrets.yaml, a file
the scanner used to skip
Another branch, started from the main branch, puts the same fake key in secrets.yaml. The scanner used to skip any file
with that name (issue #182). The commit skips the hooks with --no-verify, and the push opens merge request !2.
Its Changes tab shows the key in clear: this is what the pipeline has to catch. The test project is deleted when the
story ends.

text.tspan: git commit --no-verify -m "chore: keep the production deploy key in secrets.yaml" && git push -o

g.text: Then the pipeline of that merge request blocks the key from the pinned binary and never
prints it
The code:betterleaks job of merge request !2, from "$ task betterleaks:scan-branch" on. The job downloads the pinned
binary, checks it ("✅ Checksum verified against the published checksums.txt") and runs it with no container.
It finds the private-key in secrets.yaml and prints "REDACTED" where the key would be. Every member of the project can
read this log, and the key is not in it.
And GitLab refuses to merge it, so the key never reaches the main branch
The same page as for merge request !1. The pipeline failed, and GitLab says "Merge blocked": this project merges a merge
request only when its pipeline passed. The key cannot reach the main branch.

svg.text: Storyboard e2e · 14 steps · 14 frames · every frame is its own pixel baseline (tolerance: 0)
● Given: stage ● When: actions ● Then: proofs
